source_dependency_findings: UNAMA/OHCHR annual and midyear civilian-casualty reports are one originating monitoring system across years and cannot be counted as independent source families merely because they are separate documents.

The coded 2009 and 2011 national conflict-displacement figures in Challenges of IDP Protection are explicitly reported as UNHCR figures; they are therefore dependent on UNHCR rather than an independent displacement family for those numeric claims.
OHCHR Nepal Conflict Report 2012 states an aggregate conflict death toll but does not classify that aggregate as civilian deaths, so the aggregate was not coded into direct civilian harm.

AIHRC 2004-2005 reports property destruction and extrajudicial-killing complaint categories, but the aggregate table does not identify a clean conflict-specific civilian victim population, actor attribution, or harm pathway; those counts were not forced into the registered outcome.

A/60/343 provides important qualitative context about harm to civilians and vulnerable groups but no clean source-native quantitative record satisfying the frozen civilian-harm coding schema was identified in this pass.
immutability_note: This first-coder pass is URL/source-locator bound but not yet immutable-content bound for every newly screened web source. Blank archive hashes must remain blank until an actual archived source byte stream is acquired and hashed; a URL is not a content hash.
